weeks.title: Baseline check
weeks.intro: A short check in each track so we know where you are starting. No preparation needed — just try your best.

maths.title: Maths baseline
maths.learn: Think before you calculate — look for a pattern or a shortcut.

questions.q: What is the sum of the first 20 odd numbers (1 + 3 + 5 + … )?
questions.why: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². 20² = 400.

questions.q: How many two-digit numbers are divisible by 7?
What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 4:00?
What is the last digit of 2²⁰?
questions.why: Last digits of powers of 2 repeat 2, 4, 8, 6. 20 is a multiple of 4, so the last digit is 6.

questions.q: In how many ways can 3 friends sit in a row of 3 chairs?
Smallest number greater than 1 that leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, 3 and 4?

science.title: Science baseline
science.learn: Science questions test ideas, not memory. Ask “why?”

questions.q: Why does a huge steel ship float while a small steel nail sinks?
options: Ships are made of lighter steel
The ship’s shape pushes aside (displaces) more water than its weight
questions.ans: The ship’s shape pushes aside (displaces) more water than its weight
questions.why: Buoyancy: the hollow shape displaces a large volume of water.

questions.q: Ice floats on water because…
options: ice is less dense than water
questions.ans: ice is less dense than water
questions.why: Water expands when it freezes, so ice is less dense.

questions.q: A ball is thrown straight up. At its highest point its speed is…
options: the same as at the start
questions.why: It stops for an instant before falling.

questions.q: Which of these is a chemical change?
Turmeric indicator turns red in…
questions.why: Soap solution is basic; turmeric turns red in a base.

questions.q: You stand 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far are you from your image?
questions.why: The image is 2 m behind the mirror: 2 + 2 = 4 m.

logic.title: Logic baseline
logic.learn: Work step by step and keep track carefully — that is what programmers do.

questions.q: Find the next number: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
A robot starts facing North. It goes forward 2, turns right, forward 3, turns right, forward 2. Where is it now?
questions.why: North 2 → East 3 → South 2 leaves it 3 steps East of where it began.

questions.q: What is the binary number 1011 in our normal (decimal) numbers?
To find the largest of 8 numbers by comparing two at a time, what is the fewest comparisons needed?
questions.why: Each comparison knocks out one number; 7 must be knocked out.

questions.q: x = 1. Repeat 5 times: x = x × 2. What is x at the end?
All bloops are razzies. All razzies are lazzies. Which must be true?
“Meticulous” means…
questions.why: A meticulous person checks every detail.

questions.q: Book : Library :: Painting : ?
questions.why: Books are kept in a library; paintings in a gallery.

questions.q: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
options: Its raining, so take you’re umbrella.
It’s raining, so take your umbrella.
Its’ raining so take your umbrella
It’s raining so, take you’re umbrella.
questions.ans: It’s raining, so take your umbrella.
questions.why: It’s = it is; your = belonging to you.

questions.q: Odd one out:
questions.why: The Moon is a satellite; the others are planets.

questions.q: “Riya checked the sky, grabbed her umbrella and sighed.” What can we infer?
options: She expected rain and was not happy about it
It was a sunny day she loved
questions.ans: She expected rain and was not happy about it

questions.q: The opposite of “scarce” is…

maths.title: Divisibility & number patterns
maths.learn: Divisibility tricks: by 3 or 9 → add the digits; by 4 → last two digits; by 5 → ends in 0/5; by 11 → alternate sum. Look for patterns before calculating.

questions.q: Which number is divisible by 9?

questions.why: Fibonacci: each term is the sum of the two before: 8 + 13 = 21.

questions.q: Smallest number divisible by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6?
How many factors does 36 have?

science.title: Force & motion
science.learn: Speed = distance ÷ time. Friction opposes motion. Inertia: things keep doing what they are doing unless a force acts. Pressure = force ÷ area.

questions.q: A car travels 100 km in 2 hours. Its average speed is…
Why do we slip easily on a wet floor?
questions.why: Water reduces friction between feet and floor.

questions.q: When a bus starts suddenly, standing passengers fall backwards because of…
questions.why: Their bodies tend to stay at rest.

questions.q: The SI unit of force is the…
A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because…
options: the force acts on a smaller area, giving more pressure
it has less friction with air
questions.ans: the force acts on a smaller area, giving more pressure

logic.title: Patterns & sequences
logic.learn: Find the rule: look at differences, ratios, squares, or positions in the alphabet (A=1 … Z=26).

questions.q: Next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ?
Row 1 has 1 dot and each row has double the dots of the row above. Total dots in the first 5 rows?

english.title: Vocabulary in context
english.learn: Use the rest of the sentence to guess a new word’s meaning.

questions.q: “The teacher was lenient and let us submit late.” Lenient means…
“His explanation was so lucid that everyone understood.” Lucid means…
“She was reluctant to speak on stage.” Reluctant means…
“The ancient fort was dilapidated.” Dilapidated means…
“The crowd was jubilant after the win.” Jubilant means…

maths.title: Counting smartly
maths.learn: Multiplication principle: if one choice has a ways and another has b ways, together there are a × b ways. Pigeonhole: if n + 1 things go into n boxes, some box gets two.

questions.q: 6 people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes?
How many 3-digit numbers can be made from 1, 2, 3 without repeating a digit?
3 shirts and 4 trousers. How many different outfits?
How many numbers from 1 to 100 contain the digit 7?
questions.why: 10 ending in 7 + 10 in the 70s − 77 counted twice = 19.

questions.q: What is the fewest people needed to be sure two share a birth month?
questions.why: 12 months = 12 boxes; 13 people guarantees a shared month.

science.title: Matter & its changes
science.learn: Physical change: no new substance (melting, dissolving). Chemical change: new substance (rusting, burning). Acid + base → salt + water (neutralisation).

questions.q: Rusting of iron needs…
Which is a physical change?
questions.why: Ice → water is the same substance.

questions.q: Baking soda + vinegar fizzes because it gives off…
A solid changing directly into a gas (like camphor) is called…
Acid + base → ?

logic.title: Step-by-step instructions (algorithms)
logic.learn: An algorithm is an exact list of steps. Trace it carefully, writing down the values after each step.

questions.q: A robot faces East. Instructions: F, F, L, F, L, F, F (F = forward one square, L = turn left). Where does it end?
questions.why: East 2, North 1, West 2 → 1 square North of the start.

questions.q: x = 10. While x > 1: x = x ÷ 2 (drop any remainder). How many times does the loop run?
a = 3, b = 5. Then a = a + b; b = a − b; a = a − b. Final values?
questions.why: This trick swaps the two values.

questions.q: Searching a sorted list of 1000 words by always opening the middle, at most about how many looks are needed?
Rule: if even, halve it; if odd, × 3 + 1. Starting at 6, how many steps to reach 1?

english.title: Analogies
english.learn: Find the relationship in the first pair, then apply the same one.

questions.q: Bird : Flock :: Fish : ?
questions.why: A group of fish is a school.

questions.q: Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
questions.why: Object : what it is used for.

questions.q: Hot : Cold :: Ancient : ?
Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
Petal : Flower :: Page : ?

maths.title: Geometry thinking
maths.learn: Triangle angles add to 180°. Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles. Pythagoras: a² + b² = c² in a right triangle.

questions.q: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. The third is…
A square has area 49 cm². Its perimeter is…
Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is…
An exterior angle of a triangle equals…
options: the sum of the two opposite interior angles
questions.ans: the sum of the two opposite interior angles

questions.q: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. The longest side is…

science.title: The living world
science.learn: Leaves make food (photosynthesis) through chlorophyll; stomata let gases in and out. Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins bring it back.

questions.q: Which part of a plant mainly makes food?
Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart are…
questions.why: A for Arteries, A for Away.

questions.q: Most digestion and absorption of food happens in the…
questions.why: Villi in the small intestine absorb nutrients.

questions.q: Tiny pores for gas exchange on leaves are called…
questions.why: Mostly on the underside of leaves.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a mammal?

logic.title: Binary & secret codes
logic.learn: Computers use binary (0 and 1). Place values: 8 4 2 1. Codes replace letters by a rule.

questions.q: 5 written in binary is…
The largest number you can write with 4 binary digits is…
Each letter is shifted forward by 1 (A→B). The code “IBU” means…
How many different patterns can 3 bits (0/1) make?
If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 …, the total for “CAB” is…

english.title: Reading between the lines
english.learn: Inference = what the writer suggests without saying it directly. Look for clues in actions and words.

questions.q: “Arjun’s shoes were caked with mud and left a trail on the clean floor.” What had he probably been doing?
options: Playing or walking outside in wet ground
questions.ans: Playing or walking outside in wet ground
questions.why: Mud on shoes → wet ground outside.

questions.q: “His mother raised an eyebrow and pointed silently at the door mat.” How did she feel?
What did his mother want him to do?
options: Wipe his shoes on the mat
questions.ans: Wipe his shoes on the mat
questions.why: She pointed at the door mat.

questions.q: “Despite the heavy rain, the stadium was packed for the final.” What does this tell us?
options: The match was very important to people
questions.ans: The match was very important to people

questions.q: In that sentence, “despite” shows…

maths.title: Word problems & logic
maths.learn: Turn words into equations; check your answer makes sense.

questions.q: A father is 4 times as old as his son. In 20 years he will be twice as old. How old is the son now?
A train goes 60 km/h for 2½ hours. Distance?
5 pencils cost ₹35. 8 pencils cost…
A snail climbs 3 m each day and slips 2 m each night in a 10 m well. On which day does it get out?
questions.why: After 7 days and nights it is at 7 m; on day 8 it climbs 3 m to the top.

questions.q: A is taller than B. C is shorter than B. Who is tallest?

science.title: Light & electricity
science.learn: Light travels in straight lines. A plane mirror image is upright, same size and laterally inverted. A fuse melts to break the circuit when current is too high.

questions.q: Light travels in…
An image in a plane mirror is…
options: upright, same size and laterally inverted
questions.ans: upright, same size and laterally inverted

questions.q: Which material conducts electricity best?
A fuse protects a circuit by…
options: melting when the current is too high
questions.ans: melting when the current is too high

questions.q: A rainbow forms because sunlight is…
options: split into colours (dispersed) by water droplets
questions.ans: split into colours (dispersed) by water droplets

logic.title: Maps, networks & order
logic.learn: Networks (graphs) are points joined by lines. Shortest path = try routes and add distances. A stack is last-in-first-out; a queue is first-in-first-out.

questions.q: Roads: A–B 4 km, B–C 3 km, A–C 9 km, C–D 2 km, B–D 7 km. Shortest route from A to D?
Sort 5, 2, 8, 1 from smallest to largest. Which number is second?
A network of 6 points, all connected, with no loops (a tree) has how many lines?
questions.why: A tree with n points has n − 1 lines.

questions.q: You can trace a figure using every line exactly once when the number of points with an odd number of lines is…
Plates are stacked one on top of another. Which plate do you take first?
questions.why: Last in, first out — a stack.

english.title: Grammar & critical reasoning
english.learn: Read statements exactly — do not assume more than they say.

questions.q: Neither of the boys ___ finished the work.
She is good ___ maths.
“All students who practised daily passed.” Riya passed. What can we conclude?
options: We cannot be sure Riya practised daily
questions.ans: We cannot be sure Riya practised daily
questions.why: Others may have passed without daily practice.

questions.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The match was won by our team.
questions.ans: The match was won by our team.

questions.q: The scientist’s ___ led to a new vaccine.

roadmap.title: Discovery (12 weeks)
roadmap.text: Equal exposure to four tracks. The app tracks accuracy, enjoyment, time and consistency to show where he naturally leans.

roadmap.title: Choose 1–2 focus tracks
roadmap.text: Build foundations in the chosen tracks (Class 8–9 topics) with weekly challenges and past papers.

roadmap.title: First maths olympiad: IOQM
roadmap.text: Open from Class 8. First attempt is for experience. Route: IOQM → RMO → INMO → IMO camp.

roadmap.title: First science olympiad: NSEJS
roadmap.text: Open to Classes 8–10. Route: NSEJS → INJSO → selection camp → IJSO.

roadmap.title: Computing olympiad: ZIO / ZCO
roadmap.text: Open to any school student. ZIO needs no coding. Route: ZIO/ZCO → INOI → IOI camp.

roadmap.title: Serious attempts
roadmap.text: INMO and INJSO are realistic targets. Class 10 is the last chance for the junior science olympiad (IJSO).

roadmap.title: Senior olympiads + JEE base
roadmap.text: NSEP / NSEC / NSEB (or INMO / INOI) alongside JEE preparation — olympiad problem-solving gives a big JEE advantage.
